children: heads into Tuesday's earnings report with shares at $192.45, down 0.76% around 12.54 p.m. ET on October 19, and a cash target worth watching. Investor's Business Daily highlighted the October 20 results in its defense earnings preview. The company needs more than $4.3 billion in second-half free cash flow just to reach the bottom of its annual forecast. A huge order book helps. Turning those orders into cash is the next test.

RTX's July 23 earnings release reported first-half free cash flow of $4.187 billion and lifted the full-year target to $8.50 billion$8.75 billion. That leaves $4.313 billion$4.563 billion to generate in the second half, roughly 3%9% more than in the first. Second-quarter sales reached $24.708 billion, adjusted earnings hit $1.89 a share, and backlog stood at $289 billion. Commercial orders accounted for $170 billion, with defense contributing $119 billion.

The valuation adds pressure: shares sit 23.73% above the displayed GF Value estimate of $155.54, suggesting investors already expect solid execution. That estimate is a valuation reference, not a price ceiling. Tuesday's cash-flow figures and updated outlook will help test whether that premium has support. Watch deliveries, collections and cash conversion. More orders would be welcome, but progress toward the cash target would give investors stronger evidence that the backlog is paying off.

title: RTX Stocks Move Lower Ahead of Earnings and a $4.3 Billion Cash Hurdle
